risks.statement: The runtime condition registry defines CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN values as READY / CAUTION / NOT_READY, but the golden fixture decision trace contains readiness="STANDARD". requiredResolution: Decide whether STANDARD is a legacy fixture-only value that maps to READY.
Or update registry to include STANDARD.

risks.title: PACE_SOURCE_IN ESTIMATED path is registry-valid but never emitted
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4D.2.5 — Pace Source Evidence/Risk Alignment (deferral originally made and documented in Phase 4D.2 — PACE_SOURCE_IN Resolver Implementation)
risks.statement: The runtime condition registry defines PACE_SOURCE_IN.ESTIMATED as a valid value, but Backend Integration Phase 4D.2's PaceSourceResolver deliberately never emits it: no approved estimation methodology was found anywhere in the repository for deriving a pace source from runningBackground / recentWeeklyVolumeKm / recentLongestRunKm / recentRunsPerWeek alone. As a result, a user who supplies training-volume evidence but no recent race result and no target finish time currently resolves to NONE, not ESTIMATED. This is acceptable while the resolver remains unwired from live generation, but it is activation-relevant: before PACE_SOURCE_IN output is ever consumed by real plan generation, product must decide how this user population should be classified.
requiredResolution: Approve and document a V1 estimation methodology for ESTIMATED (e.g. from training-volume evidence), and implement it in PaceSourceResolver; or
Explicitly decide V1 will not use ESTIMATED at all and update registry/docs accordingly (e.g. mark it reserved-for-future-version); or
Keep ESTIMATED reserved but explicitly confirm product/UX accepts NONE as the outcome for training-volume-only users.
Do not implement an unapproved estimation method to close this risk.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume PACE_SOURCE_IN (not specific to any catalog candidate version)
risks.implementationNote: Backend Integration Phase 4D.5.1 (cross-risk finding, discovered during Phase 4D.5 orchestration testing): if the ESTIMATED path described above is later implemented, OR PaceSourceResolver's output priority (currently RECENT_RACE > TARGET_TIME > NONE) changes for any other reason, re-verify GoalFeasibilityResolver behavior for the combination PACE_SOURCE_IN=NONE with targetFinishTimeSeconds present. Reason: as of Phase 4D.5, GoalFeasibilityResolver's own PACE_SOURCE_NONE_TARGET_TIME_REQUESTED branch is unreachable through real RuntimeConditionResolutionService.ResolveAll orchestration, because PaceSourceResolver already emits TARGET_TIME (not NONE) whenever targetFinishTimeSeconds exists -- GOAL_FEASIBILITY_IN never sees PACE_SOURCE_IN=NONE while a target time is also present under the current pipeline. This is a behavioral dependency between the two resolvers' logic, not a type-system guarantee -- nothing prevents a future change to PaceSourceResolver's priority order (e.g. if ESTIMATED is introduced ahead of TARGET_TIME, or the priority order is otherwise revised) from making this branch reachable again with different semantics than originally intended. See PHASE4D_5_RUNTIME_CONDITION_RESOLVER_ORCHESTRATION_SERVICE.md ('a new finding') and PHASE4D_5_1_PACESOURCE_GOALFEASIBILITY_CROSS_RISK_NOTE.md for full detail. This note does not change PaceSourceResolver or GoalFeasibilityResolver behavior -- it only records the dependency for future re-verification.

risks.title: AsOfDate preview/confirm lifecycle semantics not wired
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4D.2.5 — Pace Source Evidence/Risk Alignment (field originally added in Phase 4D.2 — PACE_SOURCE_IN Resolver Implementation)
risks.statement: PaceSourceResolver computes recent-race-evidence age (and the associated recency-confidence metadata) relative to RuntimeResolverContext.AsOfDate, an explicit evaluation-date field added in Phase 4D.2 specifically so the resolver never reads the wall clock directly. However, the live preview/confirm request lifecycle does not yet supply or persist an AsOfDate anywhere -- no code populates this field outside of tests. Before any future phase wires PaceSourceResolver into live generation, product/engineering must decide: does AsOfDate get fixed at preview-generation time and then reused unchanged at confirm (for preview/confirm consistency), or does it get recomputed fresh at confirm time (allowing recency to reflect any delay between preview and confirm)? No repository evidence resolves this question either way.
requiredResolution: Decide whether confirm reuses the preview's AsOfDate or recomputes it independently.
Wire whichever behavior is chosen into the live preview/confirm flow when PaceSourceResolver is eventually connected to generation.
Do not silently default to wall-clock time at confirm without an explicit product decision.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume PACE_SOURCE_IN recency metadata (not specific to any catalog candidate version)
risks.implementationNote: Backend Integration Phase 4E.1.1 (governance clarification pass): Phase 4E.1 computed AsOfDate exactly once per preview (DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.UtcNow), never re-read per resolver) and threaded it unchanged through the pilot resolver pipeline and into the frozen CatalogPreviewSnapshot.AsOfDate field -- see PHASE4E_1_CATALOG_PREVIEW_ROUTING_AND_IMMUTABLE_RESOLUTION_SNAPSHOT.md section 7. This satisfies the preview-side half of PaceSourceResolver's own AsOfDate contract, but does NOT touch this TD's actual closure criteria, all three of which are about CONFIRM: whether confirm reuses the preview's AsOfDate unchanged or recomputes it independently, and wiring that decision in. Phase 4E.1 does not wire catalog generation into confirm at all (by design), so none of the three requiredResolution items are satisfied yet. Intended closure path: Phase 4E.2, which must read the frozen AsOfDate from the stored CatalogPreviewSnapshot at confirm time and make (and wire) an explicit reuse-vs-recompute decision -- never silently default to wall-clock time at confirm. This TD may legitimately remain OPEN even after Phase 4E.2 ships if that phase implements snapshot-reuse mechanically without an explicit, recorded product decision on which policy (reuse vs. recompute) is correct. Backend Integration Phase 4E.2 acceptance-finalization pass addendum (appended, not replacing the above; status NOT changed to closed -- reconciled per PHASE4E_2_CLAUDE_SAFETY_AUDIT.md section 17 and PHASE4E_2_FINAL_ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.md): CatalogPlanConfirmationService.BuildPlan now explicitly reads StartedAt from snapshot.AsOfDate and never recomputes it from DateTime.UtcNow (ConfirmedAtUtc is kept strictly separate, technical-only). RESOLVED by this: (a) preview freezes AsOfDate exactly once; (b) confirm code, where wired, does not recompute AsOfDate; (c) confirm does not rerun resolver orchestration to derive AsOfDate or anything else; (d) an immutable preview/confirm snapshot-consistency boundary now exists in code. UNRESOLVED, and NOT covered by this TD's own tracked closure criteria: persistable stage-to-week schedule generation (GeneratedPreviewPlanPayload is still always null -- BuildPlan's AsOfDate-reuse code is not reachable in production because the step-11 persistability guard rejects every real snapshot first, so the reuse decision has never been exercised against real traffic); calendar-day alignment (does not exist); production concurrent-confirmation safety (no DB-level preview-to-plan uniqueness invariant exists -- tracked as a Blocking Defect in PHASE4E_2_CLAUDE_SAFETY_AUDIT.md section 15, not part of this TD's own scope); and public catalog activation (still blocked by the PUBLISHED-only eligibility gate, independently of this TD). This TD is NOT closed: its own three requiredResolution items are substantively addressed by (a)-(d) above, but the repository's established convention (see TD-CORE-READINESS-001's own precedent) is not to mechanically close a risk whose implementation has not yet been exercised against real, live traffic -- the AsOfDate-reuse code path in BuildPlan has never actually run against a real confirm request. Re-review for closure once a future phase makes GeneratedPreviewPlanPayload reachable and this code path is genuinely exercised.

risks.title: CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN thresholds are not approved
risks.statement: CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN registry values exist (READY / CAUTION / NOT_READY). Phase 4B provides optional evidence fields (recentWeeklyVolumeKm, recentLongestRunKm, recentRunsPerWeek) that could in principle feed a readiness classification. No approved threshold mapping was found anywhere in the repository to convert those fields into READY / CAUTION / NOT_READY: the only evidenced threshold set (golden-fixture-v3's CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_RESOLVER, rule TEN_K_STANDARD_ENTRY: minimumWeeklyVolumeKm=20, minimumLongestRunKm=8, minimumRunsPerWeek=3) is a single pass/fail gate with no failing example and no CAUTION/NOT_READY boundary evidenced at all, its output ("STANDARD") is not even a valid registry value for this condition type (see TD-REGISTRY-001), and Phase 4A.2 already classified this exact threshold set's scope as 'D — not approved / DECISION_REQUIRED'. Backend Integration Phase 4D.3 therefore implemented CoreEntryReadinessResolver as an always-NotEvaluated placeholder — it never emitted READY, CAUTION, NOT_READY, or STANDARD under any input.
requiredResolution: Approve V1 READY/CAUTION/NOT_READY readiness thresholds, with an explicit, evidenced boundary for all three values (not just a single pass gate); or
Explicitly decide CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN will remain NotEvaluated/unused in V1; or
Update registry/docs accordingly if the intended shape differs from a three-tier classification.
Do not implement guessed thresholds to close this risk.
risks.resolutionNote: Backend Integration Phase 4D.3.1: product owner explicitly approved V1 READY/CAUTION/NOT_READY thresholds as an internal canonical decision (recorded as EV-008 in evidence-log.json; full mapping in PHASE4D_3_1_CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_THRESHOLD_DECISION_AND_RESOLVER_ACTIVATION.md). CoreEntryReadinessResolver now implements real classification logic (READY: weekly>=15 AND longest>=6; NOT_READY: weekly<8 OR longest<4; CAUTION: otherwise, including partial-evidence cases; both-missing: NOT_READY only in a GoalType=Race context, else NotEvaluated). recentRunsPerWeek remains metadata-only per the same owner decision, never a hard gate. STANDARD is still never emitted -- confirmed by test. This risk is NOT mechanically closed (consistent with this file's existing convention of never closing a risk outright, e.g. TD-WAVE5-001's own 'revisited, not closed' precedent) because a residual risk remains: the resolver is still not wired into live generation, and its output has not yet been exercised against real, live user traffic. Re-review before any future wiring of this resolver into generation.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: Any candidate whose runtime generation would consume CORE_ENTRY_READINESS_IN (not specific to any catalog candidate version)

risks.title: Phase compression and extension priorities remain unconfirmed catalog-authoring placeholders
risks.recordedInPass: Phase 4G.3B.2 generic target-week-count phase allocator governance follow-up
risks.statement: TEN_K_MASTER v6 carries CompressionPriority and ExtensionPriority values 1/2/3/4, but AUD-008 classifies the combined priority field as PLACEHOLDER_UNCONFIRMED: the ordering was invented and has no canonical product or coaching source. The golden fixture exercises only the 12-week preferred allocation and therefore cannot validate compression or extension ordering. Phase 4G.3B.2 transports and mechanically applies the authored values without claiming they are product-approved. AllocationOrderCorrectnessVerifier consequently reports DECISION_REQUIRED for feasible non-preferred allocations whose specific per-phase distribution depends on those priorities, except the order-independent 8-week and 14-week fully-exhausted boundary allocations.
requiredResolution: Obtain an explicit product/coaching decision confirming or replacing each phase's compression priority.
Obtain an explicit product/coaching decision confirming or replacing each phase's extension priority independently rather than assuming it must mirror compression order.

Update the authoritative catalog and AUD-008 governance classification through the normal versioned catalog-authoring process before treating priority-dependent non-preferred allocations as verified safe.
risks.currentRuntimeImpact: None. The target-week-count allocator and AllocationOrderCorrectnessVerifier are not called by live routing; public support remains exact-12-week only.
risks.appliesToCandidateRootsFrom: TEN_K__4D__INTERMEDIATE v10 and any descendant retaining TEN_K_MASTER v6 priority values; revisit independently for other templates
